input.rationale: First investigation of the captured hashicorp/raft snapshot (commit c0dc6a0b2c7e889f31e5ab2f7ed90ceb159acffe). It records a usable map of both core relationships (A1 qualified support for decision formation/advancement, A2 context validity and authority transfer/loss) and their connection, and fixes one obligation about the adopted-term context after finding that the network transport can drive the appendEntries term/leader update from a per-connection goroutine through the heartbeat callback. The question is registered as the first Candidate with its counterevidence and unknowns, so the obligation states a required relation without asserting a violation.

question.question: Does the transport heartbeat callback establish the election-term and known-leader context under the same serialization as the raft main goroutine, i.e. can Raft.processHeartbeat run on a NetworkTransport connection goroutine concurrently with main-goroutine RPC handling and store a current term lower than a term the node has already adopted, or replace the currently known leader?
question.importance: The adopted current term is the value against which vote granting, duplicate-vote rejection and the acceptance of newer-term RPCs are all evaluated. If a heartbeat handled off the main goroutine stores a term lower than one the node has already adopted, the node can subsequently grant a vote in a term in which it has already voted, which is the election-safety condition of Raft; the same entry point also rewrites the stored leader identity that clients and requestVote rely on. The packaged NetworkTransport/TCPStreamLayer is the production transport, so the path is on the default deployment and not only in tests.
participants: NetworkTransport connection goroutine (handleCommand heartbeat fast path)
contexts: a node in Follower state, with a heartbeat handler registered by NewRaft, receiving a heartbeat-shaped AppendEntries from a leader of term T over NetworkTransport while the main goroutine handles another RPC
a NetworkTransport whose connection-handler goroutine invokes the callback while the main goroutine is inside appendEntries or requestVote
event_paths: connection goroutine: handleConn -> handleCommand (isHeartbeat) -> heartbeatFn(rpc) -> Raft.processHeartbeat -> Raft.appendEntries -> setState/setCurrentTerm/setLeader
main goroutine: run -> rpcCh -> processRPC -> appendEntries (setState/setCurrentTerm/setLeader) or requestVote (setState/setCurrentTerm/persistVote)
vote reuse path: requestVote reads LastVoteTerm/LastVoteCand and re-grants only for the same (term, candidate), else persists a new vote for req.Term

supporting_behavior_ids.b-leader-identity: the same fast-path entry point also writes the known-leader context, which is the sibling fact consumed by vote-grant filtering and by the client API
supporting_behavior_ids.b-commit-advance: shows which later decisions depend on the adopted term context by gating commitment on commitment.startIndex

counterevidence: The heartbeat classification keeps the fast path to requests with PrevLogEntry==0, PrevLogTerm==0, no Entries and LeaderCommitIndex==0, so it cannot append log entries, advance the commit index or run processLogs, which bounds the reachable damage.

currentTerm is read and written with atomic LoadUint64/StoreUint64 on raftState, so the hazard is a lost update (read-modify-write) rather than a plain unsynchronized access to that specific field; state and leaderAddr/leaderID are also individually atomic or lock-protected.

InmemTransport ignores SetHeartbeatHandler and always offers AppendEntries to the consumer channel, so in-memory clusters do not exercise the fast path; the integ_test.go pre-vote test installs a custom handler that itself calls processHeartbeat, which shows the pattern is used but does not establish a legal interleaving.

The heartbeat fast path is documented as existing to avoid head-of-line blocking from disk IO, i.e. to be concurrent by design; if the concurrent dispatch is intentional, the defect would be that appendEntries does not uphold the stated requirement rather than that the dispatch exists.
unknowns: Whether the connection goroutine and the main goroutine can actually interleave between the currentTerm read and the setCurrentTerm write on the same node in a legal history, and therefore whether a lower term can be stored after a higher one.
Whether a stored-term regression, if reachable, can be escalated to two votes in one term given the LastVoteTerm/LastVoteCand duplicate check, or is bounded to a transient context error.

Whether NetworkTransport is expected to serialize connection goroutines with the raft main goroutine at all, or whether the requirement in api.go only means the callback must not block on the main goroutine's disk IO.
Whether the same premise exists for other transport implementations that honour SetHeartbeatHandler, since only the in-module NetworkTransport path was read.
question.trigger_rationale: Three sourced facts point at this premise and conflict: api.go states a requirement that the heartbeat callback MUST be safe to be called concurrently with a blocking RPC; raft.go's processHeartbeat comment states the opposite, that it must only be called from the main thread; and NetworkTransport.handleCommand invokes the registered callback directly on a per-connection goroutine while non-heartbeat RPCs are serialized through the single rpcCh consumer. appendEntries performs a read-compare-write on currentTerm through a plain atomic Store (no compare-and-swap) and then unconditionally rewrites the leader identity, so the premise is a concrete interleaving question rather than a generic concurrency caution.

obligation.description: Once a node has adopted and persisted election term T as its current term, no later establishment of that term context may store a value lower than T, because vote granting, duplicate-vote rejection and the acceptance of newer-term RPCs are all evaluated against the adopted value; the requirement applies to every entry point that can update the term context, including a heartbeat-shaped AppendEntries processed outside the raft main goroutine.

scope.description: A single Raft node using the in-module NetworkTransport (or any transport that honours SetHeartbeatHandler) with a heartbeat handler registered by NewRaft, while it is handling RPCs. Applies to the current-term context only, not to the log content, the commit index or the configuration.
assumptions: the node is not shut down while the RPCs are processed
the StableStore accepts SetUint64 for the CurrentTerm key, since setCurrentTerm panics otherwise
an RPC with a term greater than the adopted term is a legal event, because appendEntries and requestVote adopt it
excluded: log replication correctness and the commit-index rule (a separate obligation)
the leader-identity fact, which is tracked separately as f-known-leader
behaviour of transports outside this module that do not implement a heartbeat fast path

pending: whether the connection goroutine and the main goroutine can interleave between the term read and the term store on the same node in a legal history
whether a regressed term can be observed by requestVote soon enough to yield a second vote in an already-used term

grounding.derivation: appendEntries ignores an older term but adopts a greater one, and it writes the term with setCurrentTerm, which is a plain atomic Store rather than a compare-and-swap (s-raft-append-term, s-raft-set-current-term, s-state-term-atomic); api.go requires the heartbeat callback to be safe to call concurrently with a blocking RPC (s-api-fastpath-contract); NetworkTransport.handleCommand calls that callback directly from the per-connection goroutine instead of offering the RPC to the single consumer channel, and processHeartbeat forwards it to appendEntries (s-net-fastpath, s-net-handle-conn, s-raft-process-heartbeat); the heartbeat classification is decided inside the transport from the request shape, so the callback receives a request that nevertheless performs the term and leader writes. Since the adopted term is the value that requestVote evaluates against and duplicates are only recognised for the same (term, candidate) (s-raft-vote-record), a lower stored value would permit a second vote in a used term.
grounding.applicability: Applies when a transport runs the registered heartbeat callback on a goroutine other than the raft main goroutine, which is what NetworkTransport does for heartbeat-shaped AppendEntries; it does not apply to InmemTransport, which ignores SetHeartbeatHandler.
unresolved: whether the two goroutines can interleave between the read of currentTerm and the store inside one appendEntries call
whether a concurrent equal-term or greater-term main-loop RPC is required for the hazard, or a single heartbeat suffices
conflicts: raft.go states that processHeartbeat must only be called from the main thread while api.go states the callback MUST be safe to call concurrently with a blocking RPC
alternatives: the requirement may be read as 'the callback must not be blocked by the main goroutine's disk IO' rather than 'the callback may run concurrently'; under that reading the implementation is consistent and only the comment is stale
the atomic store may be intended to be last-writer-wins and protected in practice by the transport offering non-heartbeat RPCs to the main loop

associations.rationale: This entry point is the located implementation of the requirement: it is the callback that can be invoked from a transport goroutine yet performs the same current-term update as the main-loop RPC path.

bindings.description: Raft.processHeartbeat is the callback registered through Transport.SetHeartbeatHandler; it checks only shutdown and the command type and then forwards the AppendEntriesRequest to appendEntries, which performs the term and leader writes.
pending: whether this callback is serialized with the raft main goroutine by the transport that invokes it

result.summary: Submitted draft/submission.json (action=obligation) with draft/map-v1.json for the captured hashicorp/raft snapshot (commit c0dc6a0b). The map establishes a usable core overview over both core lines and their connection: A1 formation/advancement is grounded in the pre-vote and real vote tally, commitment.match/recalculate, and the startIndex rule that only lets a quorum match index at or past the leader's own-term first index advance commitIndex; A2 context/authority is grounded in the term/state adoption and leader-identity writes of appendEntries/requestVote/installSnapshot, checkLeaderLease step-down, and TimeoutNow transfer; the connection is sourced from the vote-record duplicate rule, the rejection of older-term RPCs, the startIndex constraint, and the requirement that a transfer target be caught up. The map carries 7 activities, 18 behaviors, 6 facts and 4 surfaces (39 cited source ranges; nested fuzzy/raft-compat modules and third-party transports recorded as deferred surfaces). The first Candidate registers one obligation, c-adopted-term-never-regresses, with binding bind-raft-process-heartbeat (raft.go processHeartbeat): the NetworkTransport connection goroutine invokes the heartbeat callback directly, and the callback re-uses appendEntries, which performs a read-compare-write of currentTerm through a non-monotonic atomic store and rewrites the leader identity, while api.go requires that callback to be safe to call concurrently with a blocking RPC and raft.go's comment states the opposite. The question is disposition=ready_for_check / preferred_check=direct_test on principal fact f-term-adopted (preservation), with the heartbeat-shape restriction, the atomic-store caveat, the InmemTransport difference and the intentional-design reading recorded as counterevidence, and reachability of the interleaving, possible escalation to a double vote in one term, and the transport's intended serialization contract left as explicit unknowns. Optional preflight with the trusted validator returned valid=true; no target code was executed and no map is claimed as accepted.

It records a usable map of both core relationships (A1 qualified support for decision formation/advancement, A2 context validity and authority transfer/loss) and their connection, and fixes one obligation about the adopted-term context after finding that the network transport can drive the appendEntries term/leader update from a per-connection goroutine through the heartbeat callback. after.purpose: Form a cluster decision and advance it legally: gather support that is qualified by the current voting configuration, and only advance the commit index for entries a quorum has stored when this leader may commit them.
after.realization_summary: A candidate becomes leader only after grantedVotes reaches quorumSize() (or pre-vote grants first reach the same quorum); a leader records each voter's acknowledged match index in commitment.matchIndexes and commitment.recalculate advances commitIndex only when the majority match index is at least commitment.startIndex, the first index created in the leader's own term. Followers advance their own commit index only from the leader's LeaderCommitIndex bounded by their own last index.

after.purpose: Keep the election-term and leadership context valid, and acquire, transfer or lose authority only through the term/leader fields that every subsequent decision is evaluated against.
after.realization_summary: Inbound AppendEntries/RequestVote/InstallSnapshot adopt a strictly greater term and drop to Follower; accepted AppendEntries/InstallSnapshot record the leader identity; requestVote/requestPreVote reject support while a different leader is known; checkLeaderLease steps the leader down when it cannot contact a quorum within LeaderLeaseTimeout; TimeoutNow moves authority by putting the target into Candidate with candidateFromLeadershipTransfer. NetworkTransport can additionally drive the AppendEntries term/leader update from a connection goroutine through the heartbeat callback.

after.purpose: Recover and resynchronize a participant that cannot be caught up by log replay, and re-establish eligible participation.
after.realization_summary: When setPreviousLog cannot find an index the leader sends the newest snapshot with sendLatestSnapshot/InstallSnapshot; the follower streams it to a SnapshotSink, restores the FSM through fsmMutateCh, then sets lastApplied/lastSnapshot/configuration and truncates logs. NewRaft restores the newest usable snapshot at start.

after.purpose: Maintain the configuration that decides who is a participant and whose support counts.
after.realization_summary: Configuration changes are accepted only while the latest configuration is committed and this leader has committed an entry of its own term; nextConfiguration derives the new configuration and checkConfiguration rejects an empty/duplicated participant set or a configuration without a voter; the new configuration is written as a LogConfiguration entry, applied to configurations.latest, pushed into commitment.setConfiguration and used to start/stop replication.

after.purpose: Apply committed decisions to the client FSM in commit order and report completion to callers.
after.realization_summary: processLogs converts committed indices into commitTuple batches (LogCommand/LogBarrier/LogConfiguration) and hands them to fsmMutateCh; the fsm goroutine applies them through FSM.Apply or BatchingFSM.ApplyBatch and responds to the logFuture, and snapshot requests report the last applied index/term.

after.purpose: Persist and reconstruct the history that support is evaluated against (term, vote, log, configuration).
after.realization_summary: setCurrentTerm and persistVote write StableStore before the in-memory state changes; dispatchLogs writes the leader's new entries to the LogStore before notifying replicators; NewRaft reloads the term, last log and snapshots and replays configuration entries from the log to rebuild configurations.latest/committed; snapshotting persists FSM state and compacts logs.

after.purpose: Expose the client contract: which node may be asked to act, what completion means, and what leader identity is reported.
after.realization_summary: Apply/ApplyLog/Barrier enqueue a logFuture and complete when the FSM path responds; VerifyLeader drives an immediate heartbeat round and completes when a quorum answers; Leader/LeaderWithID report the stored leader identity under leaderLock; CommitIndex/AppliedIndex export the internal indices.

after.execution_owner: client goroutines calling Apply/Barrier/VerifyLeader; the leader main goroutine serves applyCh/verifyCh
after.protocol_context: client-facing contract of acting as leader
after.trigger: a client call on a node that may or may not be leader
implementation_guards: a follower or candidate answers ErrNotLeader on applyCh/verifyCh/configurationChangeCh
VerifyLeader steps down when a quorum does not answer
important_branches: a single-voter cluster answers VerifyLeader immediately

after.execution_owner: commitment.match/recalculate, called from the leader's replication goroutines and from dispatchLogs for the leader's own disk write
after.protocol_context: leader-side commitment bookkeeping for the current term
after.trigger: a tracked voter's match index increases
legal_preconditions: the entry being considered belongs to this leader's term or an earlier entry has already been committed in this term
implementation_guards: commitIndex only advances when quorumMatchIndex >= commitment.startIndex
matchIndexes contains only servers with Voter suffrage from configurations.latest
important_branches: a new configuration resets matchIndexes for the new voter set and recalculates immediately
async_boundaries: the advance is published to the leader main goroutine by a non-blocking notification on commitCh

after.execution_owner: the leader's raft main goroutine (configurationChangeChIfStable, then appendConfigurationEntry) using nextConfiguration/checkConfiguration
after.protocol_context: membership change with at most one uncommitted configuration entry
after.trigger: a configuration change future is accepted while the latest configuration is committed and the leader has committed an entry of its own term
legal_preconditions: the latest configuration is committed
getCommitIndex() >= commitment.startIndex
implementation_guards: prevIndex mismatch is rejected when a different configuration has been added in the meantime
checkConfiguration rejects duplicate IDs/addresses, empty IDs/addresses and a configuration with no voter
important_branches: protocol versions below 2 translate the change into a legacy remove-peer message carrying the whole configuration

cross_activity_effects.A1: quorumSize() and commitment are recomputed from the new voter set, so the qualified support base changes with the configuration
cross_activity_effects.A2: the committed configuration decides whether the local server may keep leading or must step down

after.execution_owner: the candidate's raft main goroutine (runCandidate, then preElectSelf or electSelf)

cross_activity_effects.A4: vote eligibility is decided from configurations.latest, so a participant change immediately constrains who can be granted support

formation.explanation: Qualified support is gathered before a decision is formed. A candidate counts granted votes (or pre-vote grants) and only becomes leader when the count reaches quorumSize(); the leader then records each voter's acknowledged match index through commitment.match, and commitment.recalculate advances commitIndex only when the majority match index is at least commitment.startIndex, the first index created in the leader's own term, so entries of earlier terms are never committed on match indexes alone. Followers advance their own commit index only from the leader's LeaderCommitIndex bounded by their own last index.

context.explanation: The context that qualifies support and authority is the adopted term plus the known leader identity. Inbound AppendEntries/RequestVote/InstallSnapshot ignore older terms and adopt a strictly greater one by writing StableStore and dropping to Follower; accepted AppendEntries/InstallSnapshot then record the leader identity, which requestVote/requestPreVote use to refuse support while a different leader is known. A leader loses authority locally through checkLeaderLease when it cannot contact a quorum of voters within LeaderLeaseTimeout, and gains it at the target through TimeoutNow, which puts the target into Candidate with candidateFromLeadershipTransfer. The same term/leader update is additionally reachable from a NetworkTransport connection goroutine through the registered heartbeat callback.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the term and at the own-term replication rule. A durable vote record is only re-granted for the same (term, candidate) and is otherwise superseded once a greater term is adopted, so support gathered in term T cannot be consumed in term T+1; conversely an RPC whose term is older than the adopted term is ignored, so a deposed leader cannot re-establish authority. On the leader side, a follower's match index only becomes usable support after the leader has matched a quorum at or beyond commitment.startIndex, so pending work from an earlier term constrains what the new leader may commit; and leadership transfer explicitly requires the target's nextIndex to be past the leader's lastIndex before TimeoutNow, so an up-to-date support context is a precondition for moving authority. Because both lines read and write the same current-term context, an entry point that updates that context outside the main goroutine (the transport heartbeat callback) is the point where the connection is not obviously serialized.

open_details: The pre-vote grant path was read at the level needed for the context path; its interaction with a concurrently observed leader was not traced to completion.
Verification reads (VerifyLeader/verifyFuture) and their quorum accounting were not traced to completion; they are represented only through the client contract activity.
Snapshot-driven log truncation was read at its call sites; the interaction with a MonotonicLogStore implementation is recorded as a deferred surface.
after.rationale: Both core relationships and their connection are explained from actual code: formation and advancement are grounded in the vote tally, the pre-vote round, commitment.match/recalculate and the startIndex own-term rule; context and authority are grounded in the term/state update, leader identity update, the leader lease step-down and TimeoutNow. The connection is sourced: votes are only re-granted for the same term, older-term RPCs are ignored, match indexes are only usable at or after startIndex, and a transfer requires the target to be caught up. The one anomaly found while reading this backbone (the transport heartbeat callback that re-uses appendEntries from a connection goroutine) is recorded as a Behavior unknown and as the first Candidate rather than as a core gap, so the overview remains usable while that premise stays open.

after.meaning: The node's commit index is I: an entry at I has been stored by a quorum of the current voting configuration and may be applied to the FSM.
after.validity_context: On a leader, indices before commitment.startIndex cannot be advanced by match indexes alone, so at least one entry of the leader's own term must be replicated first; on a follower the value is min(LeaderCommitIndex, lastIndex).
representation: configurations.committedIndex when the committed entry is a configuration
after.durability: in-memory only; the FSM state may be persisted by the caller
after.recovery: not recovered across restarts; re-committed by the next leader

after.meaning: The node's durable log agrees with the leader's log through index I at term T, with any conflicting local suffix already removed.
after.validity_context: Established only after StoreLogs/DeleteRange completed on the main goroutine, or after a snapshot install placed the state at I; superseded when a later term rewrites the suffix.
after.recovery: rebuilt by InstallSnapshot or by the NewRaft log scan

after.meaning: The leader's commitment table records that voter V stores the leader's log through index I, which is the support the leader may count toward a commit decision.
after.validity_context: Usable for commitment only while V is a Voter in configurations.latest; a new configuration rebuilds the table from the old values.
after.durability: in-memory and per leader term; a new commitment is created on each leadership acquisition
after.recovery: not recovered; re-derived from the next successful AppendEntries or InstallSnapshot responses
unknowns: whether a match recorded for a peer that is concurrently removed from configurations.latest can still contribute to a commit decision before setConfiguration runs

after.meaning: The node's stored leader identity is (leaderAddr, leaderID), being the leader that last contacted it in the adopted term; the identity is used to reject vote and pre-vote requests while another leader is known and is reported to clients through Leader/LeaderWithID and Stats.
after.validity_context: Cleared by every state transition, because setState clears the leader before changing state, and replaced by each accepted AppendEntries or InstallSnapshot.
after.durability: in-memory only; not persisted across restarts
after.recovery: relearned from the next accepted AppendEntries or InstallSnapshot

after.meaning: The node has adopted election term T as its durable current term, and every subsequent vote grant, append-entries acceptance, pre-vote answer and leadership decision is evaluated against T. A vote is only re-granted for the same (T, candidate), and RPCs with a term below T are ignored.
after.validity_context: Holds from the moment T is persisted until a strictly greater term is adopted. The library's design assumes the adopted value never decreases.
after.durability: setCurrentTerm writes StableStore first and panics if that fails, then updates the in-memory atomic
after.recovery: NewRaft reloads the term from StableStore before any goroutine starts
unknowns: whether an out-of-band heartbeat AppendEntries can store a value lower than a term the main goroutine has already stored on the same node

after.meaning: The node has durably recorded the vote (T, C) for election term T; a duplicate request for the same (T, C) is re-granted from this record, and a request for a different candidate in T is refused.
after.validity_context: Holds for the adopted term T; adopting a greater term makes the record unusable for new grants because the duplicate check only matches the request term.
after.durability: persisted through StableStore before the vote is granted; a persistence error leaves the vote ungranted
after.recovery: read back on each RequestVote; not rebuilt from any other state
unknowns: whether a stored-term regression could let a second, different candidate be granted in a term in which the node has already voted

after.reason: removeOldLogs and compactLogsWithTrailing were read only at the call sites used by the snapshot behaviors; the effect of a non-monotonic store on history reconstruction is not mapped here.
The shape test on the decoded AppendEntriesRequest decides whether the RPC bypasses the main consumer channel, which is the entry point of the selected Candidate.

The interface lets a transport run the registered callback on its own goroutine; this module implements the fast path only in NetworkTransport and InmemTransport ignores the call, so the concurrency contract of other transports is unread.
These are separate Go modules with their own go.mod files and are outside the single module selected for execution.

after.system_boundary: github.com/hashicorp/raft as captured (single module; module path github.com/hashicorp/raft). One Raft instance is one node of a cluster; the module also ships NetworkTransport/TCPStreamLayer/InmemTransport, an in-memory FSM/store for tests, and the raft-compat and fuzzy nested modules. FSM, LogStore, StableStore and SnapshotStore are caller-supplied interfaces, so durability of applied state is outside this module.
